This year Chan has taken real ownership of the vendor relationships. He renegotiated three contracts and saved the company about $60,000. His documentation is thorough, and his colleagues rely on him. One area for development is delegation. He tends to do things himself instead of asking his team. I would like him to work on that in the next six months. Overall, I rate his performance as exceeds expectations.

Last year I made the worst hiring decision of my career. I hired someone with a perfect CV who interviewed brilliantly, and within three months it was clear that he did not fit with the team. It cost us roughly $40,000 in salary and lost time, and her morale. What I learned is that we had skipped the step where candidates meet the people they will actually work with. Now every finalist spends an afternoon with the team, and honestly it has made our hires better and faster. Since we introduced that, our 12-month retention has gone from 70% to 92%. If you hire people, I would encourage you to try it.
